name: suricata
description: Reads the Suricata intrusion-detection engine's alerts from its eve.json log, the one path OPNsense opens on it (data source 2), into its own table of security events, with the per-file watermark as its durable state and a lost rotation recorded as a collection gap; and resolves, after each pass, what the installed-rules grid says of the rules that fired, into its rule-info table (ADR 0020 wave 4).

settings.label: plugin.suricata.setting.rule_info_per_pass
settings.note: How many rule identities one rule-info run asks the installed-rules grid about: opnview's own, not a survey figure. Suricata's rule metadata is read one sid per request (survey, data source 2, Rule metadata), and each request runs a configd script on the firewall that opens the rule cache, so the bound caps the extra requests one alert pass makes. 25 a run resolves 1 500 distinct rules an hour, beyond what any of the rulesets the survey met fires in a day; what is not asked carries over to the next run.

settings.label: plugin.suricata.setting.rule_info_recheck_seconds
settings.note: After how long a rule's answer is asked again: opnview's own, not a survey figure. A rule's metadata changes only when its ruleset is downloaded again, which OPNsense does on the schedule the user sets on Services > Intrusion Detection > Administration, commonly once a day; asking again after a day follows such a change within one update while costing at most one request per rule per day. It applies to found and not-found answers alike, so a rule installed after it was first asked about is found the next day.

endpoints.name: query_alerts
endpoints.note: Read-only. Paging is offset-from-end-of-file and therefore unstable; the durable cursor is (fileid, filepos).

endpoints.name: alert_logs
endpoints.note: One entry per rotated file with filename, size, modified and sequence.

endpoints.name: status
endpoints.note: status of running / stopped / disabled / unknown.

endpoints.name: installed_rules
endpoints.survey_section: Rule metadata, read from source for step 6
endpoints.note: Read-only: the installed-rules grid of Services > Intrusion Detection, one rule per call, filtered by its sid. Each row carries sid, msg, rev, gid, reference, source (the ruleset file), action and enabled, plus classtype and every metadata tag the rule declares (scripts/suricata/lib/rulecache.py); no field holds the rule's priority, which is Suricata's severity.

enable_pages.label: plugin.suricata.opnsense_page.ids_administration
enable_pages.note: Services > Intrusion Detection > Administration, which holds ids.general.enabled (controllers/OPNsense/IDS/forms/generalSettings.xml).

checks.name: severity_known
checks.expression: normalised_severity IS NULL OR normalised_severity IN ('critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'informational')

checks.name: src_port_range
checks.expression: src_port IS NULL OR (src_port >= 0 AND src_port <= 65535)

checks.name: dst_port_range
checks.expression: dst_port IS NULL OR (dst_port >= 0 AND dst_port <= 65535)

checks.name: src_firewall_has_no_client
checks.expression: NOT src_is_this_firewall OR src_client_id IS NULL

checks.name: dst_firewall_has_no_client
checks.expression: NOT dst_is_this_firewall OR dst_client_id IS NULL

checks.name: severity_known
checks.expression: normalised_severity IS NULL OR normalised_severity IN ('critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'informational')

checks.name: not_found_carries_nothing
checks.expression: lookup_state = 'found' OR (normalised_severity IS NULL AND provider_severity IS NULL AND category IS NULL AND rule_source IS NULL)
